basis: Defining limb and digit malformations; frequencies of developmental delay, renal anomalies, hearing loss and ocular defects are unspecified.
Neoplasm originates in the small intestine; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Classified as a muscular channelopathy caused by a calcium-channel defect; no specific neural involvement is established.
Degenerative disease of knee articular cartilage and joint structures.
Primary carcinoma of liver cells; extrahepatic damage is not established as a common defining feature.
Benign neoplasm of ceruminous glands in the external auditory canal.
Viral infection and inflammation of the inner-ear labyrinth.
Hepatic glycogen storage and metabolic dysfunction define GSD Ia; intrinsic renal tubular/glomerular dysfunction commonly develops over time (>30%).
The concept itself denotes irreversible cochlear hearing damage caused by platinum chemotherapy.
Tumour arises in the supratentorial meninges.
Congenital profound deafness and generalized skin, hair and ocular hypopigmentation define the syndrome.
Biologically inactive growth hormone causes impaired endocrine growth signalling; short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Immune-mediated intraocular inflammation against exposed lens proteins, with frequent visual loss.
Inherited platelet aggregation defect; gastrointestinal bleeding in 1/2 reflects impaired haemostasis rather than intrinsic gastrointestinal disease.
Structural aneurysm of an intracranial artery; neural injury requires a complication and is not established across this subtype.
Skin fragility/scarring and joint hypermobility define cEDS; GI symptoms and pulp calcifications do not establish damage; aortic abnormalities occur in <30%.
Isolated spermatogenic failure and infertility affect reproductive function; elevated FSH is a feedback response, not a separate endocrine disorder.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with intellectual disability; small pituitary in 4/5 lacks documented endocrine dysfunction.
Squamous carcinoma originates in the ovary as a reproductive organ; no endocrine function or other qualifying organ involvement is established.
Vitamin K deficiency impairs coagulation factor activity; this does not itself establish hepatic injury.
OXPHOS disorder; encephalopathy/neuropathy, cardiomyopathy/arrhythmia and muscle weakness each occur in 30-79%; renal, ocular and hearing abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Developmental delay/intellectual disability commonly characterize partial chromosome 16 duplications; other malformations vary by duplicated segment.
Intellectual disability and aganglionic megacolon define the syndrome; congenital cardiac defects occur in roughly 50-60%; recurrent otitis is a separate infection.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; distal denervation atrophy and fixed foot deformities are common (>30%); cardiomyopathy frequency is unestablished.
Left renal vein compression causes renal venous hypertension, varices and collecting-system bleeding; proteinuria and haematuria occur in 30-79%.
